title: Instinct AI for Job Search: Which Connectors Find, Tailor and Apply? (2026)
summary: Instinct has no job-application feature. See which Instinct connectors help with job search in 2026, and when Tsenta could let Instinct apply.
body_markdown:
**The best Instinct connector for job search in 2026 is Google Workspace, the only service Instinct’s public pages name, which gives Instinct your email inbox and calendar so it can filter job alerts, flag recruiter replies and keep interviews on your calendar.** No Instinct connector applies to jobs for you: Instinct’s pages name no LinkedIn, job board or résumé connector, and they describe no way to add a custom connector or MCP server. Tsenta is an MCP server that connects to your AI assistant to tailor your résumé, submit applications on supported company career sites and track the replies, but it has no Instinct guide. It could work in Instinct only if your Instinct account supports custom remote MCP servers.


Published November 20, 2026. Tsenta publishes this guide and sells an applying agent. We read Instinct’s homepage, Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, Acceptable Use Policy, SMS terms, blog and sitemap that day. Instinct publishes no help center, developer docs or pricing page, and its blog says “No posts yet”, so its legal pages are the fullest public account of what it connects to. We did not use a signed-in Instinct account, and we quote Instinct only where its public pages say it.


## What Instinct is


Instinct is a personal assistant from Spear Street Technology, Inc. that you text or call. Its[homepage](https://instinct.com/) says “there are no new interfaces” and “It can use a phone and computer in the same way that you do.” Its examples are errands: ordering ingredients for a recipe, booking a train home, sending flowers to a friend. No Instinct page we read mentions jobs or résumés.


Three facts shape how you use it for a job search:


- **It is free as of November 20, 2026.** Instinct’s[Terms](https://instinct.com/terms) say it “is currently available without charge to you” and that Instinct will give notice before any fees. There is no pricing page.
- **You may wait to get in.** You sign up with your phone number at app.instinct.com. Its[SMS terms](https://instinct.com/legal/sms-terms.html) say that if you sign up while Instinct “is at capacity”, you get a welcome text when your spot opens. The homepage also has an Invite a friend link for members.
- **It acts, it does not just answer.** Its[Privacy Policy](https://instinct.com/privacy-policy) says its browser can “interact on your behalf” with websites you have not connected, and the Terms say it can “take Actions” on outside services for you.


Search results for “Instinct” also bring up a Garmin watch line and other products. This guide covers the assistant at instinct.com, which many reviews call Instinct AI.


## Instinct’s official connectors, checked November 20, 2026


Instinct calls the services you link “Connected Services”. Its[Privacy Policy](https://instinct.com/privacy-policy) , last revised November 17, 2026, names one: Google Workspace. Linking it gives Instinct access to “your instances of various Google products such as your calendar and email inbox”.


The[August 26, 2026 version of that policy](https://web.archive.org/web/20261101075823/https://instinct.com/privacy-policy) listed seven products by name: Google Calendar, Gmail, Google Drive, Google Docs, Google Sheets, Google Slides and Google Tasks. The November 17 revision dropped the list. Guides written in September and October that quote the seven products describe the older policy, which is why this guide treats Gmail and Calendar as confirmed today and Drive, Docs and Sheets as “ask Instinct”.


Instinct has two other routes into your accounts. The same policy covers services “for which you provide login credentials or other account information”, so a login you hand it counts as a Connected Service. And its browser can act on sites you never connected.


Service What Instinct’s public pages say Use in a job search


**Gmail** (Google Workspace) Named: “email inbox” Filter job alerts, spot recruiter replies, draft answers


**Google Calendar** (Google Workspace) Named: “calendar” Catch interview invites and keep times straight


**Google Drive, Docs and Sheets** Listed until the November 17, 2026 revision; now under “various Google products such as” Keep résumé versions and a tracker sheet, if your link opens them


**Accounts you give it a login for** Allowed as Connected Services A job board account, with you responsible for what it does there


**Websites you have not connected** Its browser “may also allow it to interact on your behalf” Read job posts and company pages, and possibly attempt a form


**LinkedIn** Not mentioned No connector


**Job boards and applicant tracking systems** Not mentioned No connector


**Notion, Outlook and Slack** Not mentioned Not confirmed on Instinct’s public pages


**Custom connectors or MCP servers** Not described No documented way to add Tsenta or any other job service


One user’s[October 2026 setup walkthrough](https://eliotprince.com/blog/instinct-ai-personal-assistant) lists Outlook, Notion, Slack and other connectors in Instinct’s signed-in workspace, while[eesel’s October 2026 write-up](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/instinct-ai-for-recruiting) lists no Outlook connector. We could not confirm any of them on Instinct’s public pages, so open app.instinct.com/workspace and see what your own account offers before you plan around one.


## What Instinct can do for a job search on its own


None of the uses below is a job-search feature that Instinct describes. Each one follows from what its pages say it can reach, so treat them as requests to try and check, not promises.


- **Filter job alerts.** Point saved-search alerts from LinkedIn, Indeed or company career pages at the Gmail you link, then ask Instinct to text you only the roles that fit. It reads the inbox and texts you, which is all this needs.
- **Watch for replies.** Recruiter emails, assessment links and interview invites land in the same inbox. Instinct’s Terms say it may “proactively send you messages” and “provide updates about the tasks you ask Instinct to perform”.
- **Handle scheduling.** The Privacy Policy lists “scheduling appointments” among its everyday tasks, and it can see your calendar.
- **Research companies.** Its browser can read company sites, news and job posts without a connector, which suits a one-page brief before an interview.
- **Draft from your résumé.** Instinct collects “text and documents you send to Instinct”, so you can send your résumé and a job post and ask for a tailored draft. Its Terms say it uses “third party large language models”, and no Instinct page describes résumé formatting or keyword checks, so read every line before you use it.
- **Keep a tracker.** If your Google link opens Sheets, ask it to log each role, the date you applied and the reply. Confirm the sheet exists and is current before you trust it.


Texts to try, which we wrote as examples and did not run on a signed-in account:


1. “Every weekday at 8 a.m., check my Gmail for job alerts and text me only remote product design roles that pay $120,000 or more, with links.”
2. “When a recruiter or hiring team emails me, text me a one-line summary and tell me if it needs a reply today.”
3. “I have an interview with \[company\] on Thursday. Send me a one-page brief from their website and recent news.”
4. “Here is my résumé and this job post. Suggest edits for the post and list anything you added that is not on my résumé.”


## Can Instinct apply to jobs for you?


Not as a feature. Instinct’s pages never mention job applications, and no connector it names reaches a job board or an employer’s own application site. What it has is general computer use: its browser can act on sites you have not connected, and its Terms let it “agree to or otherwise accept, on your behalf, the terms and conditions” of a site where it acts. So Instinct may attempt an application form if you ask. It does not promise to finish one.


Users quoted in[eesel’s October 2026 write-up on Instinct](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/instinct-ai-for-recruiting) report mixed results, from applications that went through to attempts stopped by CAPTCHAs. Instinct confirms neither.


If you try it, three lines in[Instinct’s Terms](https://instinct.com/terms) matter:


- “You agree that you will maintain meaningful human oversight over all Actions,” which the Terms say includes “promptly reviewing all Actions”.
- Instinct “may … make errors in performing Actions, and Actions may not always be reversible.” An application, once sent, is with the employer.
- “You are solely responsible for ensuring that any Actions Instinct takes on any Third Party Service are permitted under the terms and conditions” of that service. Read each job site’s rules before you let any assistant apply there.


Our guide to[how AI agents apply to jobs](https://tsenta.com/blog/how-ai-agents-apply-to-jobs-2026) explains the difference between an assistant driving a browser and a service built to submit applications.


## How Tsenta could add résumé tailoring, applications and reply tracking


Tsenta is an MCP server that connects to your AI assistant and to your own Tsenta account. Through it, an assistant can:


- **Find roles.** Get roles ranked against your profile from the 300,000+ company career pages Tsenta watches, with filters for location, remote or hybrid, pay, experience, job type and date posted. It can also read full job descriptions and job links you paste.
- **Tailor your résumé.** Tsenta tailors your résumé for each role in Honest mode, which rewords your existing experience, or Aggressive mode, which rewrites more freely and may stretch claims. You can also send it as written. It drafts a cover letter when the form takes one.
- **Apply.** Start applications that Tsenta submits in the cloud on supported company career sites. Each submitted application uses one from your allowance.
- **Track replies.** Report each application’s status, manage your tracker through Applied, Interviewing, Offer, Rejected and Ghosted, and read recruiter emails in your dedicated Tsenta inbox. Tsenta classifies those emails, links them to applications and updates the tracker stage when the match is confident.


You stay in control of what goes out. With résumé auto-approval off, each tailored résumé waits for your approval, and Review before submit pauses compatible employer forms after they are filled. Auto Apply, which submits eligible roles within your filters without approving each one, needs Power. On Starter and Pro you choose each role and Tsenta submits it.


Connecting an assistant is free. Your first 25 applications are free once, with no card. In USD global pricing, Starter is $19 a month for 600 applications, Pro is $39 for 1,500 and Power is $99 for 4,500, per 30-day cycle. See[pricing](https://tsenta.com/pricing) for your local price and quarterly billing.


### Is there a Tsenta Instinct connector?


Not as a documented setup yet. Instinct’s public site does not describe custom connectors or MCP servers, and Tsenta has no Instinct guide. If your Instinct account supports custom remote MCP servers, add Tsenta’s server address,` https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp` , and sign in with OAuth. Instinct publishes no connector directory, and Tsenta is not an Instinct integration.


Instinct is set to reach at least one outside service through MCP.[Zocdoc announced on October 29, 2026](https://www.zocdoc.com/about/news/zocdoc-brings-seamless-real-time-appointment-booking-to-instinct/) a partnership, “rolling out in the coming weeks”, in which Instinct connects to Zocdoc’s MCP server to book doctor appointments. Neither company describes it as a setting Instinct users can use to add their own server, and we found no Instinct announcement of a job-search integration.


If your account does offer a custom server option, know what you are granting. One approval gives the assistant every available Tsenta tool on your account, including actions that change account data: editing your profile, moving tracker entries, replying to emails and changing Auto Apply settings. Whether an assistant asks before each action depends on the assistant, not on Tsenta. Start with résumé auto-approval off and ask Instinct to show you each résumé before it approves. Once connected, these are the asks Tsenta’s[setup page](https://tsenta.com/mcp) suggests:


- “Find three new nursing jobs near Denver that fit my profile.”
- “Apply to the first one with my résumé tailored for it.”
- “What is the status of my last five applications?”


### What works today without an Instinct connector


1. **Use Tsenta from an assistant it documents.** Tsenta publishes step-by-step setup for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex on its[MCP page](https://tsenta.com/mcp) and in the[Help Center](https://help.tsenta.com/connect-claude-chatgpt-mcp) .[Claude’s help center](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp) lists custom connectors on Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise, with one on Free. In ChatGPT, applying needs full MCP support, which[OpenAI’s help center](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-connecting-custom-mcp-servers-in-chatgpt) lists on Business, Enterprise and Edu on the web. See[Tsenta as a Claude connector](https://tsenta.com/connectors/claude) .
2. **Text Tsenta itself.** Tsenta also runs on iMessage and WhatsApp. Text what you are looking for and it replies with matching roles. Reply yes to one and the application happens in the background.
3. **Let Instinct see the replies.** Mail to your private Tsenta address lands in your Tsenta inbox and is forwarded to your account email by default, and you can change where it forwards. Point it at the Gmail you linked to Instinct, and Instinct can text you when a recruiter writes back and help with the interview time. When your private Tsenta address is on your applications, Tsenta’s inbox still links replies to their applications and moves the tracker stage for interviews, rejections and offers when the match is confident.


This split plays to each tool’s strength: Tsenta finds, tailors, submits and tracks, and Instinct watches your inbox and calendar. Our guide to[tracking job applications with AI assistants](https://tsenta.com/blog/track-job-applications-ai-assistants-2026) covers the tracking half in more depth.


## Where Instinct wins, and where it falls short


Where Instinct wins:


- It costs nothing as of November 20, 2026, and you reach it by text or call with no new app to learn.
- One assistant covers your calendar, email and errands, so a job search sits next to the rest of your week.
- Its browser can work on sites that have no connector at all.


Where it falls short for a job search:


- It describes no job, résumé or tracker feature, and names no job-board, LinkedIn or applicant tracking system connector.
- Its public pages describe no way to add a custom connector or MCP server, so there is no documented way to plug in a job service yourself.
- Its Terms put review of every action on you, which matters most for an application you cannot take back.


Tsenta’s limits are worth stating too. It has no Instinct guide, it submits on supported company career sites rather than every site, and after the 25 free applications it needs a paid plan.

## Privacy checks before you give Instinct your job search


A job search puts your work history, salary expectations and recruiter emails in front of your assistant. Instinct’s[Privacy Policy](https://instinct.com/privacy-policy) and[Terms](https://instinct.com/terms) say:


- **Training.** Your content may train Instinct’s models unless you opt out at app.instinct.com/settings. Even after you opt out, content “flagged for safety review” may still be used. Items you add to Instinct’s Vault and data from Google Workspace are not used for training.
- **Disconnecting.** If you disconnect Google Workspace, Instinct stops keeping data from it. For other Connected Services, it keeps what it already collected, including what is in your conversation history. You disconnect at app.instinct.com/workspace.
- **Deleting.** Deleting your account “may take up to 90 days”.
- **Personal use.** As an individual you may use Instinct “for your personal use only”, with one account per person.


For a step-by-step look at wiring an assistant to a job search agent, see our[guide to connecting an AI job search agent to Claude or ChatGPT](https://tsenta.com/blog/connect-ai-job-search-agent-to-claude-chatgpt-2026) .


## Frequently asked questions


### What are the best Instinct connectors for job search?


The best Instinct connector for job search is Google Workspace, the only service Instinct’s public pages name. It gives Instinct your email inbox and calendar, so it can filter job alerts, flag recruiter replies and keep interviews on your calendar. Instinct names no LinkedIn, job board or résumé connector, and its browser can read job posts and company pages without one.


### Is there an Instinct connector that applies to jobs for me?


No, not as a documented setup. Instinct’s public pages name no job, LinkedIn or résumé connector and do not describe custom connectors or MCP servers. Tsenta, an MCP server that submits applications on supported company career sites, has no Instinct guide. If your Instinct account supports custom remote MCP servers, add Tsenta’s server address and sign in with OAuth.


### How do Instinct connectors help with a job search?


With Google Workspace linked, Instinct can read job-alert emails and text you only the matching roles, flag recruiter replies and interview invites, and keep interview times on your calendar. Its browser can research companies and read job posts, and it can draft from a résumé you send it. Instinct does not describe any of this as a job-search feature, so check what it does.


### Can Instinct fill in and submit job applications by itself?


Instinct has no job-application feature. Its browser can act on websites you have not connected, so it may attempt an application form if you ask, but Instinct does not promise to finish one. Its Terms make you responsible for “meaningful human oversight over all Actions” and warn that actions “may not always be reversible”, so review each one.


### Does Instinct AI integrate with LinkedIn, Gmail, Google Drive or my résumé?


Instinct integrates with Gmail and Google Calendar through Google Workspace, and its privacy policy listed Google Drive, Docs and Sheets until a November 17, 2026 revision dropped the list. It names no LinkedIn connector. There is no résumé connector either, but Instinct keeps files you send it, so you can share your résumé and ask for a draft for a job post.


### Which official connectors does Instinct AI have for Gmail, Sheets and Calendar?


Google Workspace is Instinct’s one named connector, and it covers Gmail and Google Calendar. Instinct’s August 26, 2026 privacy policy listed Google Calendar, Gmail, Google Drive, Google Docs, Google Sheets, Google Slides and Google Tasks. The November 17, 2026 version says “various Google products such as your calendar and email inbox”, so ask Instinct which ones your link opens.


### Can I connect Tsenta to Instinct?


Not as a documented setup yet, because Instinct’s public site does not describe custom connectors or MCP servers and Tsenta has no Instinct guide. If your Instinct account supports custom remote MCP servers, add[https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp](https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp) and sign in with OAuth. Today Tsenta documents setup for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex, and you can also text Tsenta on iMessage or WhatsApp.


### How much does Instinct cost, and how do I get it?


As of November 20, 2026, Instinct’s Terms say it “is currently available without charge to you”, with notice before any fees. You sign up with your phone number at app.instinct.com, and when Instinct is at capacity you wait for a welcome text. The homepage also has an Invite a friend link for members. Instinct has no pricing page.
